summary: One client asks for LTP, then Quote too, on the same equity: Firstock streams every mode on one subscription, so the mode change sends nothing upstream; V2 ticks keyed NSE:2885 give the LTP frame, then a Quote and an LTP frame per tick, and Quote alone once LTP is let go.

notes: The web publishes a topic per subscribed mode from the same snapshot (firstock_adapter.py:777-811); the desktop serves both modes from one tick.

Firstock needs no frame for a mode change (one feed for every mode): the desktop's mode_change_frames sends none, and the web's reference count sends none for a second mode of a subscribed scrip (_should_ws_subscribe).

deviations.reason: The web's Firstock adapter puts its mode number in data.mode (1, 2, 3); the desktop sends its label. data.mode follows each broker's web adapter (lead rule 2026-11-09): closed by the per-broker dialect switch.

Firstock's i_last_trade_time is in epoch seconds and the web sends it unchanged as ltt; feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop sends the trade time in ms.

The web's Quote sends oi 0 for an equity whose tick carries no open interest (data.get("i_open_interest", 0)); a value the broker did not send is left out, never sent as 0 (docs/api/websocket-streaming/quote.md, web openalgo#2376). The desktop's Quote leaves it out.
The web sends Firstock's circuit limits (i_upper_circuit_limit, i_lower_circuit_limit, /100); the desktop's common carrier drops them.
